name: Topologically Accurate Dual Isosurfacing Using Ray Intersection
definition: A method that determines the topology of an analytical isosurface within a voxel cell by using trilinear interpolation and ray intersection along specific diagonals. It optimizes computation by finding exactly one intersection point per disjoint isosurface component, except for complex features like tunnels which require multiple points.
summary: This method extracts topologically correct isosurfaces from volumetric data using ray intersection with trilinear interpolation, avoiding the ambiguities of Marching Cubes and the gradient requirements of Dual Contouring.
